'''Julian Moray Crampton''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE}} (1 November 1952 – 26 June 2019) was a British biologist and academic. From 2005 to 2015, he was [[Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[University of Brighton]].<ref name="obit Angus">{{Cite news |last= Brooke |first=Samuel |title=Professor who fought malaria and made headlines dies at 66 |language=en |work=The Argus |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/17738483.former-university-brighton-vice-chancellor-dies-66/ |date= 29 June 2019 |access-date=2022-09-30}}</ref> In the [[2015 Birthday Honours]], Crampton was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire|CBE]], for services to Higher Education.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sussexexpress.co.uk/news/chichester-midhurst-and-bognor-residents-honoured-in-queens-birthday-honours-2220176|title=Chichester, Midhurst and Bognor residents honoured in Queen's birthday honours|website=sussexexpress.co.uk|date=12 June 2015|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Crampton was born on 1 November 1952.<ref name="obit Times" /> He graduated from the [[University of Sussex]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) degree.<ref name="obit Angus" /> He undertook postgraduate research at [[Warwick University]], and completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in 1978 with a [[doctoral thesis]] titled "The control of RNA synthesis in vitro".<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Crampton |first1=Julian M. |title=The control of RNA synthesis in vitro |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.452493 |website=E-Thesis Online Service |publisher=The British Library Board |access-date=30 September 2022 |date=1978|type=Ph.D }}</ref>

==Academic career==
Crampton was a lecturer in [[molecular biology]] and [[tropical diseases]] at the [[University of Liverpool]].<ref name="obit Angus" /> He founded the Wolfson Unit of Molecular Genetics at the [[Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine]] in 1983.<ref name="obit Liv">{{cite web |last1=Stamper |first1=Sarah |title=Obituary: Professor Julian Crampton |url=https://news.liverpool.ac.uk/2019/07/01/obituary-professor-julian-crampton/ |website=University of Liverpool News |access-date=30 September 2022 |language=en |date=1 July 2019}}</ref> He was appointed to a personal chair in 1991 as Professor of Molecular Biology.<ref name="obit Liv" /> He was made head of the newly created School of Biological Sciences in 1996, and [[pro-vice-chancellor]] for regional affairs in 2000.<ref name="obit Liv" />

His research interests included the treatment of [[malaria]], and the bites of venomous snakes and spider.<ref name="obit Times">{{cite news |title=Professor Julian Crampton obituary |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/science/article/professor-julian-crampton-obituary-b2zv82mjf |access-date=30 September 2022 |work=[[The Times]] |date=30 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He is known for developing a variety of [[mosquito]] both incapable of spreading [[malaria]] and capable of vaccinating people against malaria, known as [[flying syringes]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.malariaworld.org/blogs/breakthrough-week-flying-syringes |title='Breakthrough' of the week: Flying syringes |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=www.malariaworld.org |date=19 March 2010}}</ref>

In January 2016, Crampton was appointed Chair of Council for the [[University of Gloucestershire]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.glos.ac.uk/news/pages/university-appoints-new-chair.aspx|title=University of Gloucestershire appoints new Chair of Council|website=www.glos.ac.uk|date=18 December 2015|access-date=13 May 2016|archive-date=20 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920145802/http://www.glos.ac.uk/news/pages/university-appoints-new-chair.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref>
